question: Which archaeological site shows pit dwellings and evidence of domesticated dogs during the Neolithic period?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Burzahom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Burzahom** is an important **archaeological site** located in the **Kashmir Valley**, Jammu & Kashmir, India.
 
• This site is a prominent example of the **Neolithic period** and later periods of human settlement.
 
• Evidence of **pit dwellings** has been found here, indicating the unique architectural practices of the Neolithic people.
 
• Archaeologists have discovered traces of **domesticated dogs** at Burzahom, showcasing early human-animal interaction and domestication.
 
• Other findings include **stone tools**, **bone tools**, and artifacts related to hunting and farming practices.
 
• The site also provides insights into the **social and economic life** of people during the Neolithic period.
 
• Burzahom is recognized for its cultural significance and is considered one of the few sites reflecting early settlement patterns in the **Kashmir region**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chirand**__

 __
 
• **Chirand** is a Neolithic site located in the **Saran district of Bihar**, India.
 
• This site is known for its evidence of **agriculture**, pottery, and tools made of **bone and stone.**
 
• Unlike Burzahom, Chirand does not exhibit pit dwellings or evidence of domesticated dogs.
 
 
 
• **Koldihwa**__
 __
 
• **Koldihwa** is located in the **Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh**, India.
 
• The site is significant for its evidence of **rice cultivation**, dating back to the Neolithic period.
 
• It is associated with the use of **stone tools** but lacks evidence of pit dwellings or domesticated dogs.
 
 
 
• **Hallur**__
 
 
• **Hallur** is a Neolithic site situated in **Karnataka, India.**
 
• This site is known for its evidence of **early iron tools** and agricultural practices.
 
• Hallur does not exhibit pit dwellings or domesticated dogs, which are unique to Burzahom.
